title: Types and properties of rectangles
summary: Recognize rectangle variations, see how they are related, and calculate their measurements.

blocks.body: A rectangle is a four-sided polygon (a quadrilateral) with four right angles. Its opposite sides are parallel and equal in length. A rectangle can be wide, tall, tilted, or have all four sides equal; its orientation and proportions do not change its defining right angles.

blocks.label: A square, wide rectangle, tall rectangle, and tilted rectangle

blocks.body: By side lengths, a square is the equal-sided kind of rectangle: all four sides match. A non-square rectangle has two different side lengths; it may be wider than it is tall or taller than it is wide. The word oblong is sometimes used for a non-square rectangle, but its exact meaning can vary, so check how a source defines it.

A tilted rectangle is still a rectangle when it is turned: its sides no longer look horizontal and vertical, but adjacent sides still meet at 90 degrees. Changing its size, position, or direction does not create a new geometric type. A shape with slanted sides that do not meet at right angles is not a rectangle.

Rectangles also fit into the quadrilateral family. Every rectangle is a parallelogram because both pairs of opposite sides are parallel. A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus (a quadrilateral with four equal sides). Not every parallelogram is a rectangle, and not every rhombus is a rectangle; a square is where those two special groups overlap.

Every rectangle has four 90-degree interior angles, opposite sides that are equal and parallel, and diagonals of equal length that bisect each other. In a square, the diagonals also meet at 90 degrees. In a non-square rectangle, they generally do not.

If the side lengths are length l and width w, the area counts the square units inside and the perimeter measures the distance around the boundary. The diagonal d follows from a right triangle formed by the two side lengths.

For a 6-by-4 rectangle, the area is 24 square units, the perimeter is 20 units, and the diagonal is \sqrt{52} = 2\sqrt{13} units. For a 5-by-5 square, those same formulas give area 25 square units, perimeter 20 units, and diagonal 5\sqrt{2} units. A square follows every rectangle formula; set l = w.

blocks.title: Check your understanding
blocks.body: A 3-by-8 rectangle is rotated until one side looks diagonal on the page. Is it still a rectangle? Is it a square? Find its area, perimeter, and diagonal length.
Do not confuse a rectangle with a rectangular prism: a rectangular prism is a three-dimensional solid whose faces are rectangles. A rectangle itself is flat and two-dimensional.
